title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: not to be given to Christ by the Father = not ordained by that gracious decree to obtain eternal life in and through Christ; John xvii. 9; Eph. i. 4–5
pass_a_gloss: On the contrary, what is it not to be given unto Christ by the Father, except by no means to be ordained by such a gracious decree unto everlasting life to be infallibly obtained in Christ and through Christ? Unto which also those words look, Joann. xvii. 9. I ask not for the world, but for those whom thou hast given me, because they are thine. There are therefore certain ones not-given unto Christ, not numbered in the peculiar flock of God the Father, that is, non-elect before the foundations of the world were laid, not-predestined unto the adoption of sons according to the benevolent affection of the Divine will, Eph. i. 4, 5, etc.
pass_b_english: On the contrary: what is it not to be given to Christ by the Father, except this — not to be ordained by that gracious decree to obtain everlasting life infallibly in Christ and through Christ? Those words look the same way (John xvii. 9): I ask not for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because they are yours. So there are some not-given to Christ, not numbered in God the Father's peculiar flock — that is, non-elect before the world's foundations were laid, not predestined to the adoption of sons according to the benevolent affection of the divine will (Eph. i. 4–5, etc.).
source_text: E contra, quid est non dari Christo a Patre, nisi tali gratioso decreto ad vitam aeternam in Christo et per Christum infallibiliter obtinendam minime ordinari? Quo etiam spectant illa verba, Joann. xvii. 9. Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro iis quos dedisti mihi, quia tui sunt. Sunt igitur quidam non-dati Christo, non numerati in peculio Dei Patris, hoc est, non-electi antequam jacerentur mundi fundamenta, non-praedestinati in adoptionem filiorum pro benevolo affectu voluntatis Divinae, Eph. i. 4, 5, etc.
